You set a appointment and went through a buzz in door security system and then have a sit down with your designer. From there you go through the layout you want and stone types. If she's awesome, she'll accept any ring, no matter the stone. Find something that seems to fit her personality. If you go the diamond route, along with antique shops or pawn shops, you can search "divorce" in the for sale section of craigslist. Many people are trying to just get rid of their sets, and offer them at a steep discount (I've seen $5000 rings going for $1500). You can also search "estate jewelry" but that may be a bit pricier. But, if you want to do her birthstone instead of a diamond, you may be able to find something in the estate jewelry. May local jewelers will also do consignment for estate jewelry, but again, expensive.

You can also ask relatives, many inherit old rings from their grandparents or aunts. That's how my fiance picked out my ring. It was free, he had a couple to choose from, and it surprisingly fit, so no re-sizing needed. If you can find an older ring it will more likely be a genuine stone with a strong setting.

Finally, there are jewelers online who will help make custom rings that you can buy from directly. So, if you find something you like at Kay or some other national jeweler brand, you may save a couple hundred having a similar one made. The metal of the ring affects the price more than the stone, unless it's a really rare stone (I regularly shop for russian alexandrite rings/gemstones, but I'm pretty sure that will never happen for me).
Go to a pawn shop. You can get real gems at a lower price than a regular retail store.

So I was watching a show and the character was getting into miniatures, like figurines and cities and such. I got to thinking about it because I've always had a small interest in minitature cities and trains and the like, and it hit me.

What if you combined a city-sim like SimCity or Cities:Skylines, with real life miniatures and cities. You could use an overhead projector to project people, cars, and whatever you want on the roads, which could be colored or tagged to be recognized by the projector, technology that already exists. You could basically have a real life progression system where you physically place road systems and buildings (that don't get recognized by the projector and integrated into your game unless you can "afford" them), and get to watch you city grow right before your eyes without all the tedious boredom of clicking through dozens of submenus and dragging stuff onto a screen.

Imagine being able to "check on your city" with your eyes and hands, being able to let it run in real time while you are away and at accelerated rates when you're playing. You could have a living, thriving, dynamic city on your table.
